title: Removing 16 distant events cuts the Monte Cristo cloud variance rise by 94.5% in a magnitude-2.5 sample on days 1 to 30
abstract: We tested spatial change in fixed USGS catalogs after Monte Cristo and Ridgecrest. We compared days [1,10) and [10,30), with magnitude at least 2.5. At Monte Cristo, RMS spread about the event center rose from 12.43 to 19.42 km within 100 km. Within 50 km, it rose from 10.52 to 11.08 km. The daily bootstrap interval for the latter ratio was 0.930 to 1.187. Removing 16 distant events reduced the cloud variance rise by 94.5%. Twelve late distant events formed a western group at distances of 78.21 to 81.90 km. Magnitude and block checks retained the main boundary effect, but sparse high-magnitude intervals depended on the block model. Ridgecrest is a reference check that extends an earlier campaign test. The distant-group analysis is exploratory. This fixed-data influence result does not identify triggering, background activity, or fluid flow. The package includes both source snapshots, hashes, code, derived tables, figures, and independent arithmetic checks.
